summary: Well-executed, transparency-minded preregistered paired study that archives comprehensive artifacts. The empirical finding is narrowly scoped: a bounded generate–verify–repair (GVR) guard produced a negligible repair-on-same-candidate improvement over ungated gpt-5-mini outputs on the curated emulator-grounded confirmatory set (baseline 199/200, guarded 200/200). The study follows preregistration, archives artifacts, and appropriately limits generality. No fatal scientific flaws were found, but the manuscript should incorporate a small set of clarifications drawn from the supplied artifacts to improve interpretability and reproducibility.
required_revisions: Add a concise, explicit description in the Methods of the deterministic validator deterministic_netops_validator_v5: summarize its core parsing/normalization rules, the principal validation checks (what constitutes validation_before.valid vs validation_after.valid), key violation codes or rule classes used by the scorer, and the scoring rule name ('full_intent_constraint_validation'), citing the archived validator trace artifacts (e.g., execution/scoring/* and execution/execution_manifest.json). This content must be drawn from the archived artifacts and limited to a short paragraph that fits the five-page constraint.

Explicitly state, using artifact-backed numbers, that the preregistered power calculation assumed a baseline success ≈0.50 (the 15 pp target effect premise) and that the observed baseline success (199/200 = 0.995) deviates substantially from that assumption; add a one-paragraph statement in Results/Discussion clarifying how this realized ceiling effect affects the interpretation of the preregistered hypothesis test and the practical null result (i.e., the confirmatory run was not informative for detecting the originally targeted 15 pp effect because the baseline was near ceiling). Reference the preregistration (SHA-256) and the condition_summary.csv artifact for counts.
optional_revisions: Briefly summarize per-task difficulty counts (easy/medium/hard/very_hard) from execution/task_manifest.jsonl (already archived) to help readers assess task mix and why the baseline may have been near-ceiling.

State more explicitly the rationales and trade-offs of the shared-initial-generation estimand versus the independent-resampling estimand in a single-sentence boxed note (to reduce potential reader confusion about the interpretation of 'guarded' gains).

Expand (if space allows) the one-sentence description of the repair prompt/heuristic used when the deterministic validator invoked a repair (drawn from repair provider trace), so readers can judge the repair's mechanistic scope; otherwise point to the exact repair trace path and SHA-256 in the manuscript.
